artifacts.summary: Five-phase plan implementing research Option (ii): amend summary-format.md to admit '## Plan Deviations' as a recognized optional section and state that the required-section list is a minimum rather than a whitelist; sync validate-artifact.sh comments with zero enforcement change; add a direct summary-format.md reference plus a full summary skeleton to cslib-implementation-agent.md; align cslib-implementation-hard-agent.md Stage 6; then empirically verify zero errors and zero auto-repaired fields.

memory_candidates.content: Agent-system failure mode: when an agent definition omits an @-reference to a format standard, the agent does not fail loudly -- it improvises headings into the vacuum and trips downstream format validators. The diagnostic tell is a validator reporting missing REQUIRED sections (heading replacement) rather than rejecting extra ones. Corollary about validator design: validate-artifact.sh only reports missing required fields/sections and never enumerates a document's headings against a whitelist, so extra sections have always been silently accepted. A section that is widely used but undocumented in the standard is therefore an ambiguity in the written spec, not a live gate failure -- diagnose which of the two you have before choosing between 'conform the outlier' and 'formalize the practice'. A base/hard agent asymmetry (hard variant references the standard, base variant does not) recurs across extensions and is worth checking as a pair whenever one is found.
